wesley7.text: Above all sing spiritually. Have an eye to God in every word you sing. Aim at pleasing him more than yourself, or any other creature.

erb_questions.text: Are the words doctrinally sound? Is the text Biblical? Does it stimulate spiritual thought? Does it properly instruct? Does it inspire high spiritual ideals? Does the music fit the text? Is it excellent? Does it fit the need? Does it produce a wholesome response? Do harmful associations come to mind because of the musical style or the composer's name?

erb_first.text: The first step in planning a worship service is to have a quiet time with the Lord, asking Him to lead and direct you as to what should be accomplished

erb_format.text: Many times a familiar format for the service is more effective than a program that is different merely for the sake of variety.

erb_peaks.text: Emotional peaks occur naturally (and should not be artificially manipulated)

erb_theme.text: It is easier to start with the theme of the message and work your music from that.

mac_music_not_worship.text: Music will play on your emotion, music will stir your emotion, but that is not necessarily worship. Music will give expression to love, it will give expression to adoration, it will give expression to honor, it will give expression to worship, but it doesn't produce it. What produces it is the truth in the heart and the work of the Spirit of God.

mac_music_means.text: Music is a means to express worship, but it is not worship.

mac_congregational.text: congregational singing is simply all of us stimulating one another to love and good works.

mac_scripture_worship.text: the more Scripture you know, the more doctrine you know, the more worship you give.

mac_prayer_highest.text: If prayer is anything, it is the highest form of worship that an individual can participate in, because prayer is saying, "God, Your name, Your kingdom, Your will be elevated, not my will, not my kingdom, not my name."

barrows_hymn.text: There is not a situation in life where there isn't a hymn and a Scripture to meet the need.

graham_thank.text: Begin when you pray by thanking and praising God for His love and goodness.

graham_confess.text: Then confess your sins and ask for His forgiveness. Finally, bring your concerns to Him. You may find it helpful to keep a list of people for whom you are praying.

graham_talking.text: Prayer is simply talking to God—and the most important thing I can say about this is that God wants you to talk to Him!

graham_privilege.text: don't look on prayer as a burden or obligation; instead, look on it as a privilege.

sankey_gospel.text: D. L. Moody of Chicago will preach the gospel, and Ira D. Sankey of Chicago will sing the gospel in Bethesda Chapel every afternoon and evening this week, except Saturday, at 3 and 7 o'clock.

spurgeon_praise.text: There is no engagement under heaven that is more exalting than praising God, and however great may be the work which is committed to the charge of any of us, we shall always do well if we pause awhile to spend a time in sacred praise.

spurgeon_nuance.text: I would not wish to prefer one spiritual exercise before another, else I think I would endorse the saying of an old divine who said that a line of praise was better than even a leaf of prayer

calvin_heart.text: the spiritual songs cannot be well sung save from the heart

calvin_gift.text: the unique gift of man is to sing knowing that which he sings.

graham_barrows.text: His uncanny ability to lead a Crusade choir of thousands of voices or an audience of a hundred thousand voices in a great hymn or Gospel chorus is absolutely unparalleled
